title: My demo is finally live, looking for feedback!
author: rainbooow
selftext:
Hi everyone,

A few weeks ago I posted the trailer for Tinymon Tactics, the game I’ve been developing for about a year. In short: a solo TFT with roguelite elements, set in a Pokémon-like universe. 

The main feedback last time was that combat needed more polish, so I worked on that: hit reactions, shadows under units, and clearer VFX.

The playtest is now open on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5387050/Tinymon\_Tactics/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5387050/Tinymon_Tactics/) (click “Request Access” on the store page and you’re in).

I’d especially love feedback on:

* Is combat readable now? Can you tell what’s happening and why you won or lost?
* Does the core loop feel good?
* Do the camp upgrades (i.e. the roguelite aspect) between runs make you want to start another run?

Any other feedback is welcome too, including bugs (balance is still very much in progress).

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Feedback: 

 \- The presentation is overall impressive. There are extremely strange performance problems sometimes on the world map, particularly when it comes to transitions... it makes me wonder if you're not properly caching assets for your game's state machine? 

 \- The combat is overall legible, yes. 

 \- I cannot tell why I lost battles, no. Like, I ran into a group of enemies and they just mulched my team and I clearly had no chance. I did not have any realistic opportunity to go fishing for duplicate intellectually distinct 'mons to star-up. I was surprised that losing once like this just fully ended the run. 

 \- No, the core loop does not feel good. In this type of autobattler, the player needs some kind of health resource that they can try to protect or aggressively spend, or the fundamental mechanics just don't work. Like... without a health resource, how can I try different strategies for evolving a team? If a loss is an instant game over, then you need a completely different approach to team building because the player can't fish for duplicates, can't try to hyper-roll, can't Fast 9, etc etc etc. All you can do is roll for duplicates and hope. That's not much fun. 

 \- No, the camp upgrades did not make me want to start a new run. A meta progression system can't compensate for a broken core loop. 

  
If you want the one-and-done experience, that's fine. If you want the Teamfight Tactics experience, that's also fine. 

These things don't work together. Pick one and build the game systems around it in a complementary fashion.
